LESSON: WRITING 7.5.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.5: Writing 7.5.1 Functional writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 7.5.1 Functional writing, part of Strand 7 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to write different types of formal letters?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify the appropriate format and content of complaint, request and inquiry letters for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 7.5.1 Functional writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. write letters of complaint, request and inquiry in varied situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 7.5.1 Functional writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. acknowledge the role of letter writing in effective communication. ● in groups, learners are guided to search online using digital devices with assistive technology and offline for samples of letters of complaint, request and inquiry, ● in groups, learners are guided to discuss the content, format and language use in letters of complaint, request and inquiry letter. ● in groups, learners are guided to write letters of complaint, request and inquiry using the information from the search online/offline, ● in pairs, learners are guided to review letters from peers. Why is it important to write different types of formal letters? 90

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 7.5.1 Functional writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify the appropriate format and content of complaint, request and inquiry letters for effective communication,

   Writing 7.5.1 Functional writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. write letters of complaint, request and inquiry in varied situations,

   Writing 7.5.1 Functional writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. acknowledge the role of letter writing in effective communication. ● in groups, learners are guided to search online using digital devices with assistive technology and offline for samples of letters of complaint, request and inquiry, ● in groups, learners are guided to discuss the content, format and language use in letters of complaint, request and inquiry letter. ● in groups, learners are guided to write letters of complaint, request and inquiry using the information from the search online/offline, ● in pairs, learners are guided to review letters from peers. Why is it important to write different types of formal letters? 90

   Writing 7.5.1 Functional writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 7.5.1 Functional writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Creativity and imagination: The learner undertakes group tasks and gains new perspectives on how to do things as they search

online and offline for samples of letters of complaint, request and inquiry.

Values:
Responsibility: The learner engages in assigned roles and duties as they discuss the content, format and language use in letters

of complaint, request and inquiry letter.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Health promotion issues: The learner addresses gender related issues concerning popular sports as they search online and

offline for samples of letters of complaint, request and inquiry.

Suggested Learning Resources

● Print texts

● Braille texts

● Electronic reading materials

● Digital devices with assistive technology

● Audio visual clips

Suggested Skills:

● Identifying the appropriate format and content of complaint, request and inquiry letters for effective communication.

● Writing letters of complaint, request and inquiry in varied situations.
